Channel and descending-bank floodplain polygons and centerlines

Source: R/cross_section_regions.R
cross_section_regions.Rd

Partition reviewed inundation into three hydraulic review regions and derive independent polygon centerlines using Voronoi skeletons. These geometric artifacts are flow-direction proxies, not hydraulic flow calculations.

cross_section_regions(
  flowline,
  channel,
  floodplain,
  centerline_spacing_m = 2,
  smoothing_refinements = 2L
)

Arguments

flowline

One projected XY LINESTRING, directed downstream to upstream.

channel, floodplain

Nested, hole-filled sf polygon footprints.

centerline_spacing_m

Maximum polygon-boundary vertex spacing in metres for Voronoi construction. Existing boundary vertices are preserved.

smoothing_refinements

Number of Chaikin corner-cutting passes, 0 to 10.

Value

A list with region_polygons (three multipart parent features), regions (components), skeletons, raw_centerlines, centerlines and diagnostics. Each polygon component retains its own region_id. Disconnected components are never joined. Centerlines run downstream to upstream to match the input Flowline; descending-bank labels refer to the opposite direction.

Details

The extended directed Flowline splits the outer floodplain before subtraction of the channel. GEOS projection and a local directed tangent classify each resulting overbank component. centerline::cnt_skeleton() extracts Voronoi geometry without polygon simplification; cnt_path() selects a skeleton route between its downstream/upstream projection extremes. Ties prefer maximum boundary clearance, then coordinate order. A separate cartographic proposal uses Douglas-Peucker simplification at half the boundary spacing followed by smoothr Chaikin smoothing. Proposals that leave their polygon or become nonsimple are rejected, retaining the raw path with a flag.
